text:
We recently had the pleasure of dining at Fume RestoBar, in Brantford and it was truly an exceptional experience from start to finish.

While I don’t often write reviews, this visit certainly warranted recognition. From the moment we arrived, we were warmly welcomed by a friendly and attentive hostess. The service throughout the evening was impeccable—our wait staff were both professional and genuinely engaging, contributing to a relaxed and enjoyable atmosphere.

The culinary experience itself was outstanding. Each dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented, showcasing both creativity and quality.

The desserts deserve special mention—the Crème Brûlée and cheesecake were absolutely outstanding and provided the perfect ending to an already remarkable meal.

A particularly memorable touch was the owner, Ted, taking the time to visit our table personally to ensure we were enjoying our meal. This level of care and attention to guests truly sets this establishment apart.

Overall, our dining experience was second to none. I would highly recommend Fume RestoBar to anyone seeking exceptional food, service, and hospitality.

text:
My wife and I have been to fume several times and we have enjoyed some good meals while there. However, after last night, I left feeling let down.
Being somewhat familiar with the menu, we had already made up our minds what we were going to have before we even got there. I had a hamburger and fries and my wife decided she was going to have fish and chips. We also thought we would start with a Saganaki as she would end the meal with Toberlone cheesecake. For me, the whole meal lacked imagination and i left feeling like I didn’t get the best value for my money.
First off, I decided to have what they called their anniversary hamburger which was supposed to have been a nod to the owner’s Greek origins. When I heard that one of the specials was a feta burger, I was excited. Having been to Greece before, and the fact that I make my own feta burgers at home I thought this would be a real treat. What arrived was anything but.
First of all the feta wasn’t in the burger, but rather on the burger in two big pieces. Not only would it have been better had the feta actually been in the burger, but putting it on the burger, just made it a mess to try and eat. Note to the chef, mixing the feta in the burger, takes away some of the saltiness and leaves the cheese nice and creamy. Otherwise it was a rather bland burger. The truffle fries were just okay. The other disappointment was the Saginaki. It’s not unusual to put a light dusting of flour when making this delicious appetizer. However, for some reason they breaded the cheese, which in my mind absolutely ruined it. My wife had the fish and chips which she enjoyed.

I realize that times are tough for restaurants, but I couldn’t get over the cost of a glass of wine at $20 for a 9 ounce glass of Ripasso. My wife had a couple of blueberry teas and I had a Manhattan to start the meal. I was quite surprised that the cost for fish and chips, hamburger and fries with a few drinks would be $188 before tip. In total, a $230 meal, including tip.
The one thing I took away from this experience is that it is just not worth going out anymore to have dinner. The costs are almost extortionate and the quality and creativity just isn’t there anymore. Sadly, good places in Brantford are becoming few and far between. Hopefully you’ll feel differently when you visit Fume
